assertion.en: If every constituency had the same population and one seat, each vote would carry about the same weight in choosing an MP.

reason.en: The weight of one vote in choosing an MP depends on how many people share that MP.

b.en: Both statements are true, and here the second does explain the first: equal numbers of people give equal shares of one MP.

c.en: The assertion is true. Equal populations give each vote about the same weight.

d.en: The reason is true. One of 5 lakh has more weight in choosing an MP than one of 25 lakh.

explanation.en: Both are true, and the reason explains the assertion. One vote matters more when fewer people share the MP, so equal populations give votes about equal weight.

hints.en: Compare one voter among 5 lakh with one voter among 25 lakh.
